## Appearance

Priscilla is a pale, spiritual-looking maiden with fair features. When dressed for visiting, she appears golden and fair in silk attire.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v2 c20 P22](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0022)_

## Personality

Though appearing spiritual and pale on the surface, Priscilla is full to the brim of mischief, pranks, and fun. She is imaginative, thoughtful, and ambitious, possessing a teasing sense of humor that enjoys poking fun at others. She works hard and persistently at her studies.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c6 P12](../source/v03-c06.md#nw-v03-c06-p0012), [v3 c35 P28](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0028)_

## History

Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard, becoming close friends with them. While a student, Mr. Phillips wrote verses dedicated to her. After graduating, she taught school at Carmody before taking her own home school. During this period, she wrote a paper on cemeteries for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and arranged a visit to Green Gables with her famous aunt, Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan. After obtaining her father's consent, she entered Redmond College with Anne Shirley, and the two boarded together during their freshman year. In her sophomore year, Priscilla moved into Patty's Place along with Anne, Philippa Gordon, Stella Maynard, and Aunt Jamesina. During her summer break, she went to Avonlea to visit Anne at Green Gables. In her final year at Redmond, she focused her studies heavily on classics, preparing alongside her housemates for graduation.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P68](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0068), [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v2 c1 P57](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0057), [v2 c6 P5](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0005), [v2 c15 P23](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0023), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v2 c20 P22](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0022), [v2 c20 P24](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0024), [v3 c1 P21](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0021), [v3 c3 P10](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0010), [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c10 P52](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0052), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c23 P1](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0001), [v3 c35 P28](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0028), [v3 c37 P9](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0009)_

## Quotes

> I would wish to be famous  <sub>[v2 c13 P34](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0034)</sub>

> Is that Gilbert Blythe over there, Anne? How he has grown up this past year! He was only a schoolboy when I taught in Carmody. And of course that’s Charlie Sloane. He hasn’t changed—couldn’t! He looked just like that when he was born, and he’ll look like that when he’s eighty. This way, dear. We’ll be home in twenty minutes.  <sub>[v3 c3 P15](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0015)</sub>

> I suppose they’ll take them off when they really begin to trot, but I know they’ll take their knitting with them everywhere. They simply couldn’t be parted from it. They will walk about Westminster Abbey and knit, I feel sure. Meanwhile, Anne, we shall be living in Patty’s Place—and on Spofford Avenue. I feel like a millionairess even now.  <sub>[v3 c10 P36](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0036)</sub>

> Think of having a real live author at Patty’s Place  <sub>[v3 c36 P8](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0008)</sub>
